title: Free Will and the Problem of Evil
welcome_lead: If God is good, why is there evil? And do we really choose our actions?
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure exploring free will and the problem of evil.

walkthroughs.body_html: If God is all-powerful and all-loving, why is there evil and suffering? This is called the problem of evil. Religious people give different answers — some say God allows it to test us, others say it is the price of free will.

Free will means we can choose our own actions. Many religions teach we have free will and are responsible for our choices. Some philosophers argue everything is determined by previous causes — this is determinism.

One answer to the problem of evil is the 'free will defence': God gave humans free will to choose good or evil. Without free will, real love and goodness would not exist. Evil is the price we pay for genuine choice.
